title: VPC minimal egress allowlist and staged operator upgrade policy
creator: Maya Hernandez
description:
Problem statement: Customers in highly regulated environments require a minimal egress posture (implicit deny with explicit allowlist) while still receiving operator upgrades and critical security patches. Current Private/VPC upgrade flows assume outbound connectivity for artifact fetches or mirror-based syncs; several customers have requested a documented, tested policy for zero-or-minimal-egress environments and an operator-driven, staged upgrade choreography that can run in air-gapped or strictly proxied networks.

Goal: Define a product-level contract that specifies: (1) the smallest possible network allowlist (by endpoint, port, and protocol) for supported upgrade modes; (2) a staged operator upgrade policy that supports online, mirror-assisted, and fully offline (physical-media or airgap sync) upgrade paths; (3) acceptance criteria and QA tests that validate operator behavior under partial-network failures and strict egress policies.

Out of scope: Implementation engineering tasks for the runtime itself (ENG will break into follow-ups). This ticket is the PM-owned requirements / acceptance criteria and runbook that will be used by Solutions and Engineering during customer onboarding and release certification.
acceptance_criteria: A1: The allowlist document explicitly lists minimal required outbound endpoints, ports, protocols, and DNS resolution needs for three supported upgrade modes: online, mirror-assisted, and offline. Each entry includes a fallback rationale and expected timeout/ retry semantics.

A2: The operator upgrade policy defines staged rollout steps (canary percentage, regional sequencing, operator health probes, automated rollback windows) that operate correctly when only allowlist endpoints are reachable or when only mirror endpoints are available.

A3: For air-gapped/offline customers, the acceptance criteria include an operator-driven artifact import flow (signed artifacts) that completes without outbound egress and produces clear verification signals (checksums, signatures, operator metadata) in the cluster logs.

A4: A documented test matrix with automated CI test cases that simulate: (a) no external egress, (b) allowlisted egress only, (c) intermittent DNS resolution, and (d) slow network with large artifact fetch times. All tests must pass in release verification stage before GA for the release private-vpc-2026.04.

A5: The runbook includes escalation steps for Solutions/SRE: how to detect failed allowlist entries, how to enable a temporary operator proxy/relay, and how to perform a manual image import with exact commands and expected logs.
A6: Security review sign-off documented and KMS integration notes included for artifact signing and verification in the offline flow.
A7: UX/Docs produce a concise 'one-page' allowlist cheat sheet plus a detailed guide for blocked customers; both reviewed by Legal/Compliance and UX PD.
A8: Customers using the minimal allowlist should be able to declare compliance to their auditors using the provided checklist and logs produced by the operator during upgrade events.
A9: Updated telemetry in Console shows per-upgrade egress attempts and a flag for 'upgrade-mode' used (online / mirror / offline) for post-release monitoring.

A10: Backwards compatibility: clusters currently on private-vpc-2025.x must be able to perform a staged upgrade to private-vpc-2026.04 using the documented flows without schema changes to customer operator CRDs.
tasks: Draft initial allowlist (security & infra to validate endpoints + ports)
Define staged operator rollout policy and canary thresholds
Create offline artifact import runbook with signed-image verification steps
Design CI tests to simulate egress-limited environments
Review doc with Legal/Compliance and Solutions Engineering
Prepare 'one-page' customer cheat sheet and longer technical guide
Add telemetry events and Console flag for upgrade-mode
Coordinate engineering spike to validate operator behavior under DNS timeouts
Collect customer feedback from 3 pilot customers and iterate
qa_plan: QA-1: Automate test harness that toggles a network proxy to block all egress then gradually enables allowlist endpoints; verify operator progresses through upgrade steps and emits expected events.
QA-2: Run mirror-assisted upgrade test: simulate internal mirror with signed artifacts and verify checksum/signature checks pass and operator state transitions to 'Upgraded'.
QA-3: Offline import test: execute manual image import using runbook steps; validate logs contain verification markers and cluster reports a successful upgrade.
QA-4: Chaos test: simulate DNS resolution delays and ensure operator backoff and retry policy adheres to SLO and does not trigger unsafe rollbacks.
QA-5: Console telemetry: confirm that post-upgrade, Console shows egress_attempt_count, upgrade_mode, and last_successful_image_signature for the cluster.
QA-6: Security test: verify that artifact signature verification fails for tampered images and that operator refuses to install them with a clear audit log entry.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Documentation and CI tests (internal verification)
Phase 1: Beta pilot with 3 pre-vetted customers (mirror-assisted + offline) - Solutions to run upgrades with Solutions Engineer on call
Phase 2: Controlled GA for new Private/VPC customers with feature flag enabled and a 30-day observational window
Phase 3: Fully GA with 'minimal-allowlist' cheat sheet in onboarding and automated validation checks in Console
rollback_plan: If operator health probes fail >5 minutes post-stage in canary, automatically revert to previous operator image using documented CRD rollback command
If mirror sync verification fails, fall back to staged operator that uses previously-synced artifacts and pause further rollouts
For offline customers, provide a signed rollback bundle and manual import steps in runbook; Solutions + SRE to coordinate
decision_log: 2026-02-28: Decided to support three explicit upgrade modes (online, mirror-assisted, offline) rather than attempting a single universal flow. Rationale: simpler operator logic per mode and clearer allowlist requirements. (PM forum)
2026-03-03: Security: require artifact signing for mirror-assisted and offline imports; KMS/HSM note added. (Security review)
2026-03-07: Telemetry decision: add 'upgrade_mode' flag and 'egress_attempt_count' metric to Console to help Ops during pilots. (Telemetry sync)
2026-03-09: UX: create one-page cheat sheet for auditors and a longer technical guide for Solutions Engineers. (Docs review)
notes: Pilot customer candidates: BankAlpha (EU), HealthCo (US), GovData (APAC). Prioritize BankAlpha for mirror-assisted validation.
Engineering spike requested: validate operator behaviour when IP allowlist is used but DNS for allowlisted hostname is blocked (customer reported this in RMA-21).
Consider adding an 'operator-proxy' sample deployment for customers who can open a single outbound proxy to a vetted mirror rather than general egress.
Estimate assumes existing mirror tooling can be reused; if not, add separate engineering task for mirror manager service.
